status: written before opening August outcomes; a retrospective holdout, not a prospective bank trial
population: All official August 2026 archive rows with a narrative of at least ten whitespace-separated words; sort by receipt date and ID. Exclude exact and near copies against the original historical study and June and July eligible narratives and earlier accepted August rows. No product-, company- or outcome-based sampling.
scorer: unchanged original 0.8 TF-IDF + 0.2 CatBoost model, June recalibration and June per-destination cutoffs from locked_policy.json
compare: same gates plus hold for <50 words; July-suggested rule fixed before August counts
eligibility: An absent institution always forces review. In CFPB data the recorded recipient is only a proxy for known mailbox; no imputation into a release decision.
primary: counts routed and wrong, coverage, misroutes/routed, two-sided 95% Wilson intervals for each rate, aggregate and by destination. A zero denominator means unavailable. Confidence in local release requires one-sided exact bounds <5% after Bonferroni across two desks on an independent local sample.
shortlist: For manual holds under the length-guarded rule, rank the seven calibrated product labels. Report top-1 and top-2 hit rates, compare against two globally most frequent June 1-7 labels fixed before inspecting the held-out month. Top-2 is assistance potential, not correct human decisions or measured minutes saved.
fallback: If August has insufficient eligible narratives (no held cases, or fewer than 100), report archive availability and exact counts; do not fit another policy or pretend a test exists. Evaluate shortlist on the already-opened July cohort as a retrospective analysis. Demonstrate a registered randomized local pilot for decision quality and timing.
economics: Same scenario: four saved minutes per auto route, $30/hour, 10% spot audit, $25 incremental rework; omit fixed and rollout costs from variable value. No savings claim from shortlists.
